summary: Add OpenClaw/Polaris edit marker to footer
details: Small HTML comment in index.html footer to verify end-to-end editing and deployment from Raspberry Pi via OpenClaw.

summary: Create Polaris public and private dashboards
details: Added public Polaris activity dashboard at polaris.html and initial private dashboard shell at /private/index.html for Cloudflare Access gating.

summary: Redesign public Polaris dashboard with grouped, collapsible log
details: Updated polaris.html to add overview cards, per-day collapsible panels, and light animations, plus dedicated CSS in assets/css/polaris.css.

summary: Add Polaris TODO section to private dashboard
details: Extended /private/index.html with a visible Polaris TODO list summarizing pending work like wiring live Pi status, finishing Cloudflare Access, and future dashboard ideas.

summary: Add README documenting portfolio + Polaris architecture
details: Created README.md explaining that this repo backs devrobotics.dev, is managed by an OpenClaw agent (Polaris) on a Raspberry Pi, and includes a high-level system design + process flow for changes.

summary: Add disclaimer noting README is maintained by Polaris
details: Appended a disclaimer to README.md with a warning icon explaining that the README was drafted and is maintained by the Polaris agent running on the Raspberry Pi via OpenClaw.

summary: Fix clipping on long Polaris log entries
details: Increased the max-height on open day panels in assets/css/polaris.css so long descriptions are no longer visually cut off at the bottom of the card.

summary: Add sidebar link from portfolio to Polaris dashboard
details: Updated index.html sidebar navigation to include a direct link to /polaris.html so it feels like a first-class part of the site.

summary: Add scrollable bodies to daily Polaris log panels
details: Changed the open state of polaris-day-body to use a fixed max-height with overflow-y:auto so long day logs can be scrolled inside the card instead of being visually clipped.

summary: Revert main sidebar to original layout
details: Restored index.html sidebar navigation to the original five-section layout (Introduction, Current Research, Featured Projects, At a Glance, Contact) and removed the Polaris Dashboard link to keep the portfolio section visually unchanged.

summary: Add global header with theme toggle and logo
details: Introduced a persistent site-header on index.html, polaris.html, and main project pages with a left-aligned light/dark theme toggle and right-aligned logo (images/icon.png), wired to a small script that remembers the chosen theme via localStorage.

summary: Switch header background to solid black for visibility
details: Updated .site-header to use an opaque black background and slightly larger top padding so the new global header bar stands out clearly above the dark page background.

summary: Refine devrobotics site layout, theming, and Polaris integration
details: Converted the main site to a light/dark theme with a global top nav, updated the hero to reflect Hardik's role at Amazon Robotics, rewrote the graduate UAV research section into concise bullet points, aligned Polaris with the new layout (including a Powered by Polaris & OpenClaw section), and applied consistent header + theme behavior across project detail pages.

summary: Adjust Polaris change log panel height
details: Tuned the CSS for .polaris-day-body.open to use viewport-based min/max heights so each change log day opens to a larger, more readable box (~30–70% of the viewport) while still allowing scrolling for very long days.

summary: Highlight Polaris assistant in hero text
details: Updated the main hero section to mention Polaris as a personal assistant running on a Raspberry Pi using OpenClaw, helping maintain the site and automate workflows.

summary: Default site theme to dark mode
details: Changed the theme initialization logic so that dark mode is the default when no preference is stored, while still respecting light/dark choices via localStorage across the home, Polaris, and project pages.

summary: Format Polaris change log dates with full day and time
details: Updated polaris.html to format change log dates as full strings like 'Saturday, March 14th 2026 | 12:34 PM' both in the Latest Activity panel and in each entry's metadata.

summary: Wire Raspberry Pi status into Polaris dashboard
details: Added an auto-generated JSON snapshot (polaris-pi-status.json) with Pi metrics like CPU temperature, load, disk usage, and OpenClaw gateway status, plus a Python script (update_pi_status.py) that refreshes the JSON and pushes changes. Updated polaris.html to read this static JSON so the public Polaris dashboard shows live-ish Pi status.

summary: Tidy Pi status display and add pulsing online indicator
details: Refined the public Polaris dashboard Pi status card to use a pulsing green dot next to the Online label, separate lines for host/CPU/load/disk/OpenClaw/updated fields, and a human-friendly formatted timestamp instead of the raw ISO string. Also tightened the OpenClaw status summary in the JSON to avoid exposing IPs or other sensitive details.

summary: Make Pi status indicator more visible
details: Increased the size of the Pi status dot, added a white border and stronger glow so the pulsing Online indicator stands out clearly against the dark card background.

summary: Add RAM usage to public Pi status dashboard
details: Extended the Pi status JSON and Polaris dashboard to include RAM usage (used/total) alongside CPU temperature, load, and disk usage. The Pi-side script now parses `free -h` into a friendly RAM string and the dashboard renders it on its own line.

summary: Simplify Pi status dot styling for remote site
details: Removed the inline bullet character and white border from the Pi status dot, leaving a single glowing green circle rendered via CSS so that both localhost and the deployed GitHub Pages site use the same simple, cache-friendly styling.

summary: Switch Pi load display to CPU percent
details: Changed the Pi status backend to derive a rough CPU utilization percentage from the 1-minute load average and core count, exposing it as cpuPercent in the JSON. Updated the public dashboard to label CPU temperature as 'CPU Temp' and show 'CPU Load: X%' instead of a raw load-average number.

summary: Add detailed load breakdown to CPU load display
details: Updated the Polaris dashboard Pi status card so that the CPU Load line now shows both the percentage utilization and a breakdown of the 1m/5m/15m load averages in the format 'CPU Load: X% | Load: 0.02 (1m) · 0.05 (5m) · 0.04 (15m)' when available.

summary: Add Flower Tracker section with webcam snapshot
details: Created a Flower Tracker section on the Polaris dashboard that shows a periodically-updated image captured from the USB webcam on the Raspberry Pi. Added an auto-update script (update_flower_snapshot.sh) that grabs a frame to images/flower-latest.jpg, writes flower-tracker.json with a timestamp, and commits/pushes changes. Wired polaris.html and CSS so the latest snapshot and 'Last updated' time render nicely.

summary: Darken and auto-contrast flower snapshots
details: Adjusted the flower snapshot pipeline to run each captured frame through Pillow: first apply a stronger auto-contrast with a higher cutoff, then reduce brightness to ~80%. This pulls back overexposed highlights in the Flower Tracker images while keeping the processing lightweight and robust.

summary: Add password-gated lighting control section
details: Added a private Lighting Control section to polaris.html with a simple password gate and UI buttons for bright white (cool vs warm) and common brightness levels (25/50/75/100%). This panel is front-end only for now; actual Govee floor lamp control continues to run on the Pi via Polaris scripts and the Govee API.

summary: Add On/Off buttons to lighting control panel
details: Extended the password-gated Lighting Control section on polaris.html with explicit On and Off buttons for the Govee floor lamps, alongside existing color temperature and brightness controls. The panel remains UI-only; real lamp control is handled on the Pi via Polaris.

summary: Add Pi lights API backend and wire dashboard buttons
details: Created a small Flask-based lights_api.py on the Raspberry Pi to expose /api/lights/power, /api/lights/brightness, and /api/lights/preset endpoints backed by the Govee OpenAPI (with both H607C floor lamps). Added a systemd service (lights-api.service) to keep it running and updated polaris.html so the password-gated Lighting Control buttons call this API on http://polaris.tailaf1119.ts.net:5000.

summary: Hide Flower Tracker heading on Polaris dashboard
details: Updated polaris.html so the Flower Tracker section no longer shows the "Flower Tracker" heading or descriptive text, keeping only the live snapshot block and metadata. The underlying image update pipeline and JSON wiring remain unchanged.

summary: Retire OpenClaw runtime; move lights API into site repo
details: Uninstalled the OpenClaw gateway from the Pi to free ~1.4 GB. The lights API now runs from a .venv inside devrobotics-site, with the Govee key moved to ~/.config/polaris (outside the repo). Removed the OpenClaw status check from update_pi_status.py and the dashboard, added a .gitignore, and repaired a corrupted local git repo.

summary: Remove theme template leftovers and an 11.7 MB junk file
details: Deleted the unused HTML5 UP demo pages (elements.html, generic.html), a stray Font Awesome.webarchive from images/, and the commented-out demo contact form with placeholder address from index.html.

summary: Secure the lighting controls and stop publishing Pi-side code
details: The lighting panel now uses an access token checked by the Pi instead of a password in the page, and talks to the lights API over HTTPS on the private tailnet only. The Pi scripts (lights API, status and flower updaters) moved out of this repo so they're no longer served on the site, and the unused /private page was removed. README updated to match.

summary: Show the Pi as offline when its status goes stale; hide flower tracker without a camera
details: The Pi Status card now shows Offline (with a last-seen time) if the Pi hasn't reported in 15 minutes, instead of always saying Online. The Flower Tracker section hides itself when there's no snapshot from the last 6 hours, and the snapshot script now skips cleanly when no webcam is connected.

summary: Fix the mobile layout
details: On phones the header is now a compact bar with a swipeable nav row, so it no longer covers the top of each page. YouTube videos scale to the screen instead of a fixed 1008px width, and the homepage headshot is centered. Shared fixes live in a new assets/css/site.css.

summary: Consistent theme, favicons and pinch-zoom across all pages
details: All pages now share one theme script (assets/js/theme.js), so the dark/light choice no longer flips when moving between the homepage and project pages. Every page now has the site favicon, and pinch-to-zoom is allowed on phones.

summary: Shrink project images by 90% and add alt text
details: The three homepage project images went from 5.2 MB to about 490 KB total (resized for web, same look). They now have descriptive alt text, and clicking an image opens its project page instead of jumping to the top.

summary: Fix missing icons with a single self-hosted Font Awesome 6
details: Icons on the Polaris dashboard and project pages were blank because the site mixed an old Font Awesome 5 copy with an account-specific kit that only the homepage loaded. Replaced both with one self-hosted Font Awesome 6 Free, loaded the same way on every page.

summary: Update Pi status every 15 minutes instead of 5
details: The Pi's automatic status commits were most of this repo's 34,000+ commits. It now reports every 15 minutes, and the dashboard marks it offline after 35 minutes without a report.

summary: Load project videos only when played
details: Project pages showed up to five full YouTube players at once. Each video is now a lightweight thumbnail labeled with its real title; the player loads (privacy-enhanced youtube-nocookie) only when you press play. Without JavaScript the thumbnail links to YouTube.

summary: Add search and link-preview basics
details: Every page now has a description, canonical URL and Open Graph/Twitter tags, so links shared on LinkedIn, iMessage or Slack show a proper title, summary and image. Added robots.txt, a sitemap, and a custom 404 page that matches the site.

summary: Clean up project heading markup and credit the theme
details: The At a Glance project titles used headings nested inside italic/underline tags with a hardcoded dark red color that was hard to read in dark mode; they're now proper headings styled per theme. Added the HTML5 UP design credit to every footer, as the theme's CC BY 3.0 license requires.

summary: Rewrite the About section
details: Replaced the bullet list with a short story of how I got into robotics, from Project Jatayu at RV College to an M.S. in Robotics at Northeastern and Amazon Robotics, plus a Path timeline and a Toolbox of the tools I use.

summary: Add a Polaris project write-up
details: New page polaris-project.html explains how Polaris works: the Raspberry Pi 5 hardware, an architecture diagram, how it edits the site, reports its health, controls the lights over a private network and runs the flower tracker, plus lessons learned. The homepage has a new Polaris project card linking to it.

summary: Redesign step 1: new design foundation
details: Started the site redesign on a separate redesign branch. Added design tokens for a monochrome plus light-blue theme in light and dark (following the visitor's system setting, with a toggle that remembers the choice), self-hosted Inter and JetBrains Mono, a 12-column grid, and a new nav that hides on scroll with a mobile menu. A style guide page previews every component and is kept off the live site.

summary: Redesign step 2: bento-grid homepage
details: Rewrote the homepage as a full-screen hero followed by a bento grid: About, Polaris live, Graduate Research, four project cards, At a glance counters with the mini projects, Skills and Contact. The text is condensed from the old page and marked as draft for review; the long project write-ups move to the project pages.

summary: Redesign step 3: LiDAR point-cloud hero
details: Added a Three.js point cloud behind the homepage: a LiDAR-style terrain with a sweeping scan line that dims as you scroll, and morphs into a shape for each project card on hover (bounding boxes, the Eclipse hexacopter, a flow field, a Raspberry Pi board, a flight path). Slow devices step down in quality instead of losing it, and reduced-motion or no-WebGL visitors see a still image.

summary: Redesign step 4: motion and interaction layer
details: Added scroll reveals, a soft spotlight glow on cards, a crosshair cursor that locks onto links and cards, magnetic buttons, smooth scrolling, count-up counters, a typed-out latest log line, and page-to-page view transitions. Everything switches off for touch devices or reduced motion where it should.

summary: Redesign step 5: Polaris live tile on the homepage
details: The homepage now shows Polaris's status (online, stale or offline), CPU temperature, load, memory, disk, the latest change and how long ago it reported, refreshed every minute from the same status and log files the dashboard uses.

summary: Redesign step 8: new 404 page
details: Replaced the 404 page with a 'signal lost' scope panel: a scan line sweeping a faint point grid, the missing route in a readout, and links back home, to the projects and to Polaris.

summary: Redesign step 6: shared project page template
details: Rebuilt the Object Detection, Eclipse, Optical Flow and Polaris write-up pages on one template: a hero image that morphs in from its homepage card, a sticky key-facts sidebar, short numbered sections, click-to-play video grids and previous/next links. Every report, PDF and video from the old pages is kept.

summary: Redesign step 7: new Polaris dashboard
details: Redesigned this dashboard: a status card with online/stale/offline states, 24-hour CPU temperature and load sparklines (they fill in once the status file carries history), this log as a terminal-style timeline, the flower camera, and a restyled lighting panel that works exactly as before.

summary: Keep 24 hours of Pi status history
details: The Pi status updater now keeps a rolling 24-hour history (one sample every 15 minutes, up to 96) of CPU temperature and load in polaris-pi-status.json, which feeds the new dashboard's sparklines. Existing status fields are unchanged.

summary: Redesign step 9: final copy approved
details: Applied the owner's copy review: the hero tagline now includes photography and videography, the research summary and its sensing and flight facts are more precise, and the At a glance section keeps two counters (featured and mini projects). All other condensed text was approved as drafted.

summary: Remove the old HTML5 UP template
details: Deleted the HTML5 UP Hyperspace theme now that every page uses the new design: its CSS, Sass, jQuery plugins, scripts, Font Awesome files and the template licence. Since none of the template remains, its footer credit is no longer needed. The README describes the new file layout.

summary: Redesign step 10: faster first paint and lighter images
details: Hero text now animates in with CSS instead of waiting for scripts, cutting the homepage's mobile load time from about 7.5 s to 3.3 s. Added smaller WebP versions of the project photos, headshot and logo with responsive srcsets, stopped downloading the hidden fallback image, removed a mobile layout shift in the nav, and added a 1200x630 link-preview image.

summary: Add a small hidden surprise
details: Something for the curious. It loads only when found, so it costs regular visitors nothing.

summary: Redesign step 10: accessibility fixes
details: From the accessibility audit: the mobile menu now moves keyboard focus into its links and closes when focus leaves it, small hero text keeps its contrast over the point cloud on phones, the Polaris architecture diagram stays legible on phones by scrolling sideways, cards reveal instantly when reached by keyboard, and animated counters and the typed log line read their final text to screen readers.

summary: Redesign step 11: the new site is live
details: Merged the redesign into main: the point-cloud homepage, the shared project pages, the new Polaris dashboard and 404 page, the light and dark theme, and every fix from the final performance and accessibility checks.

summary: Build Frames, a photography section
details: Added Frames: a square three-column photo grid with a Note and Place on hover, a lightbox with a camera-viewfinder overlay and full Shot details, long-form Story pages with photos, clips and videos, and a publishing pipeline that strips photo metadata without touching the pixels, keeps HDR, and makes sharp web sizes. Frames is linked from the navigation; photos go live once the image host is set up.

summary: Publish Frames with the first photos and story
details: Frames is live: eight photos from Gujarat, Jaipur, Colorado, Arkansas, California and a flight past Mount Rainier, and the first story, about pumpkin season and student days at the smallest Trader Joe's. Photos are served in high quality from frames.devrobotics.dev, with Shot details for each.
